dataset_family: Iran Dementia and Alzheimer's Association (IDAA) clients plus volunteers, Tehran, Iran; single-centre, not public (read from the recovered text extract, not the mapped PDF)
method_family: Kinect V2 skeletal gait analysis: single-task walking, dual-task walking (counting backward) and dual-task cost features; ANFIS, logistic regression and SVM classifiers
what_it_shows: The mapped PDF is the wrong paper. The map entry points to 1-s2.0-S1746809421000963-main.pdf, which is San-Martin et al. 2021, an EEG working-memory paper (BSPC 66:102499). No PDF of the right paper (Seifallahi et al. 2022, BSPC 71:103195, 'Detection of mild cognitive Impairment from gait using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system') exists under downloads/. I did find a text extract of the right paper at C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/.kilo/worktrees/yellow-macaw/pdf_extract_114.txt: title, authors, 70 MCI / 80 HC, Kinect V2 and ANFIS all match the block. I read that extract in full up to the References. It contradicts the statement. Single-task gait already separated MCI from HC on 7 of 26 parameters, including gait velocity (55.83 vs 47.26 cm/s, p < 0.001), step time, step velocity, cadence, stride time and stride velocity. Dual-task walking raised this to 11 of 26 parameters, and dual-task cost separated the groups on no parameter at conventional significance. The only other result is the classifier comparison: DTW features gave higher ANFIS accuracy (93%) than STW features (86.87%).
why: Recorded as no for two reasons. (1) Per the verification rule, the mapped PDF is the wrong paper (an EEG study by San-Martin et al.), and the source PDF of the paper the block describes is not in the repository. (2) Independently of that, the recovered text extract of the right paper shows that the unloaded measure does NOT fail. Single-task gait velocity, step time, step velocity, cadence, stride time and stride velocity all separate MCI from HC (p < 0.001 to p = 0.0025). The dual-task condition only widens a difference that already exists, and dual-task cost itself separated nothing. The statement requires the loaded measure to separate MCI where the corresponding unloaded measure does not. Here both separate, so this is a gradient, not a dissociation. The block's 'dual-task features were more discriminative' is a classifier-accuracy comparison, which is not the statement's claim. Further caveats: the MMSE (static screen) also separated the groups (29.4 vs 26.17). Table 1 reports ages of 68.03 +/- 3.44 vs 73.43 +/- 4.72 with p = 0.16, which is implausible for n = 80/70; the single-task gait-speed difference may partly reflect age. The extract prints '<' as 'D' (Elsevier glyph mangling): 'D0.001' decodes to '< 0.001' by the paper's own footnote 'Significant difference at P D0.05'. The recovered extract has no page markers, so the page numbers below come from the extract's running headers (journal page numbers). No shared cohort, site or authors with any current supporter or other candidate. Not a preprint.

Detection of mild cognitive Impairment from gait using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system Mahmoud Seifallahi ... The study included 70 elders with MCI and 80 healthy control (HC) elderly subjects'

In total, 7 gait parameters from 26 extracted gait parameters for STW resulted in a significant difference between MCI and HC groups. These gait features included the average values of gait velocity (gait speed), step time, step velocity, step frequency, stride time, stride velocity, as well as the variability of stride time regularity.
Table 3: 'General Gait velocity (Cm/S) 55.83 +/-12.75 46.53 +/-18.68 47.26 +/-8 36.32 +/-6.82 D0.001* D0.001*' (HC STW, HC DTW, MCI STW, MCI DTW, p STW, p DTW; 'D' is the extract's rendering of '<')

Although the results of descriptive statistical analysis showed no significant difference for DTC of gait parameters between MCI and HC subjects, there were levels of differences between the two study groups.
